entries.title: Confirm Send no longer lists every additional contact under CC
entries.summary: With **Include additional contacts of recipients (CC)**, each recipient's additional contacts are copied on that recipient's own email. **Confirm Send** used to merge all of them onto one **CC** line, so a bulk send looked as if every email copied everyone. The **CC** line now shows only the addresses copied on every email, and the per-recipient copies appear as a count: "Additional contacts: N people CC'd on their own contact's email". Delivery was always correct; only the dialog changed.

where.path: Contacts or Sessions → select records → Send → Send Email → Include additional contacts of recipients (CC) → Review → Send Now

entries.use_case: A program team emails 120 speakers with each speaker's assistant CC'd. Confirm Send now reads "Additional contacts: 120 people CC'd on their own contact's email", not a CC line of 120 assistants that makes it look like every assistant gets every speaker's email.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer worries that a bulk email CC'd every additional contact on every message, or hesitates at Confirm Send because the CC line looks wrong.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who email speakers or contacts with their additional contacts (assistants, co-authors) CC'd.
internal.staff_path: Event → Contacts → select records → Send → Send Email → Include additional contacts of recipients (CC) → Review → Send Now
internal.gotchas: Display-only: emails always went out with each contact's own additional contacts only. A manually typed CC, or a CC that lands on every email, still shows on the CC line. With one recipient everything is listed as before. In Sessions → Select Individual Contacts, only checked recipients are counted. Reported by Clarion (event 6018, SB-10102).
internal.talk_track: What you see at Confirm Send now matches what goes out: each assistant is copied only on their own speaker's email.

entries.title: Session Catalog: choose a Catalog, Timetable or Agenda program layout — with a session panel, People directory and Add to calendar
entries.summary: A Session Catalog gallery now has a **Program layout** setting in the Design tab: **Catalog** (filter rail beside session rows grouped by day and time), **Timetable** (rooms across, start times down, colour-coded by track, with a Grid / List toggle) or **Agenda** (day tabs and expandable rows with Now / Next / Ended chips). Switching is instant in the preview. All three open the same session panel — date, time, room and time zone, abstract, speakers with bios, the presentations inside a symposium, **Save**, **Copy link** and **Add to calendar** (calendar file, Google Calendar, Outlook). A **People** tab adds a faculty directory with person pages. Sessions without a start time collect under a **TBA** day. The **Your brand** theme now keeps a neutral canvas and uses the brand colour for navigation and buttons, and the Site's font is loaded on every gallery.

enable.path: CMS → Content Galleries → a Session Catalog gallery → Design → Program layout

where.path: CMS → Content Galleries → a Session Catalog gallery → Design → Program layout / Navigation tabs → People

entries.use_case: A scientific congress with six rooms and three days wants attendees to scan the day room by room the way they do on the printed grid, and a single-track summit wants a phone-friendly agenda. Both are the same Session Catalog; the organizer picks Timetable or Agenda in Design and the published program, the session panel and Add to calendar come with it.

cs_action.note: Existing Session Catalogs keep the Catalog layout (the previous rows, now with the toolbar and day grouping). Offer Timetable to multi-room programs and Agenda to single-track or mobile-first ones; check the People tab is on if the customer wants a faculty page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer compares our program page to cAttendee, Oxford Abstracts or a custom program site, asks for a room-by-time grid, a day-tab agenda, speaker bios in the program, a faculty list, or Add to calendar on sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Content Galleries preview customers publishing a Session Catalog — medical and scientific programs first.
internal.staff_path: Org → CMS → Content Galleries → a Session Catalog → Design → Program layout; super users can flip Demo mode (account menu) to preview every layout with a generated congress.
internal.gotchas: Timetable falls back to the list under 1024px and on the TBA day. Add to calendar appears only on sessions with a start time. Demo mode data shows only in the builder preview (preview token), never on the public URL. Program strings are English-only until the fr/es/de gallery translations ship. The Your brand theme change affects every gallery on that preset — the canvas is no longer the brand primary.

entries.title: Brella is generally available, and Apps is open to anyone who manages integrations
entries.summary: Brella no longer needs Sessionboard to add it: open **Apps** in the left sidebar, choose **Brella** under **Engagement**, and connect it yourself. **Apps** in the organization sidebar now shows to anyone who can view integrations, not only Sessionboard staff, and organization **Settings > Integrations** opens Apps.
entries.use_case: A customer running their event app on Brella can connect it the same day without a support ticket: their admin opens Apps, adds the Brella token and organization ID, and maps each Sessionboard event to a Brella event. Admins who used to go to Settings > Integrations land on Apps automatically.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for Brella, asks where Settings > Integrations went, or reports that Apps was locked for their admin.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations that use Brella for networking or content, and any admin who manages integrations.
internal.gotchas: LiveBuzz is still added by Sessionboard on request. Brella refuses a timeslot outside its event dates, so line those up before the first sync. Nothing is deleted in Brella: a speaker who leaves the accepted set comes off the timeslot and both records stay.
internal.talk_track: Brella is now a self-serve app. Open Apps from the sidebar, connect Brella with your token and organization ID, map your event, and sync.

entries.title: See every email an event will send before it goes out
entries.summary: **Email Campaigns → Upcoming sends** lists the next 7, 14 or 30 days of automatic email: scheduled and recurring campaigns, upload slot, acceptance, call for papers and awards reminders, the speaker feedback release, and date-based automations. Open a send to see each recipient and the email they will get, with a warning when it reaches people on unaccepted sessions. Two automatic sends that were failing now go out: date-based automations that skipped enrolled contacts, and the awards submission deadline reminder.
entries.use_case: Before a reminder goes out, a program manager can check exactly who receives it and what it says, and catch a send that would reach speakers on pending or declined sessions, instead of finding out from a confused speaker afterwards.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why someone got (or did not get) an automatic email, or wants to check reminders before a deadline.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event team using reminders, scheduled campaigns or automations.
internal.gotchas: The recipient list shows the first 500 people. Automations with no fixed time are listed separately as sends that fire when triggered.
internal.talk_track: Upcoming sends is one list of everything the event will email on its own. Open any send to see who gets it and preview the message.
